sentences.text: Dicksonosteus was a member of the class Placodermi, an extinct group of armored fish. It is most closely related to the genera Arctolepis and Heintzosteus.

This animal possessed a wide, flat body and relatively feeble jaws compared to later arthrodires like Dunkleosteus. Exceptionally preserved fossils from Spitsbergen reveal details of its braincase and internal anatomy.
The genus Dicksonosteus was described by Goujet in 1975.
Its feeble jaws suggest Dicksonosteus was a benthic fish that ate smaller, softer-bodied animals.
Dicksonosteus was once classified as an actinolepid but is now placed in the family Phlyctaeniidae.
Dicksonosteus lived during the Early Devonian period in Spitsbergen, Norway. Its existence spanned the Pragian to the Emsian stages, occurring between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
